I am an old woman, seventy-nine years, and I farm this small piece of maize near my home. My back is not what it was, and I have no money to buy the fertilizer from the shop — one bag is too much for my small plot and too dear for me. I will do what I have always done: put the manure from my few chickens and the ash from the cooking fire on the soil, plant the seed I saved from last harvest, and weed with my hoe when my grandchildren can help me. The rains here in Mbeya are good, so I do not worry too much, but I cannot spend money I do not have.
